extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers (SROs), research administrators, and grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of NIH policies, procedures, and topic-specific reviewer guidance governing the peer review and scoring of research grant applications, including initial SRG review, second-level Council review, conflict-of-interest rules, human-subjects/inclusion requirements, and scoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process — initial and second-level review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of applications for support from the NIH takes place in multiple steps. The initial peer review takes place in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) that are composed mainly of scientists from the extramural research community. The second level of peer review is carried out by the NIH National Advisory Councils or Boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review: SRGs (study sections) are managed by Scientific Review Officers (SROs). CSR manages SRGs that evaluate most investigator-initiated applications; Institutes and Centers' Review Branches manage SRGs that evaluate applications submitted in response to RFAs and other unique programs. Second-level Councils ensure NIH receives advice from a cross-section of the US population during deliberations and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosters of Scientific Review Groups availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Rosters of the membership of NIH Scientific Review Groups are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency of SRG composition: applicants and the public can consult SRG rosters. Additional information about application referral & peer review can be found on the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) web site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated criteria for evaluating research grant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Announces Updated Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications (see NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-05-002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and comparisons between updated and previous criteria are provided in linked documents: 'Comparison Of Updated And Previous Criteria For Evaluating Research Grant Applications' and 'Questions and Answers about the Updated NIH Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications.' Reviewers should consult these documents for the specific evaluation dimensions and how they differ from prior guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR Scoring Procedure (referenced as a procedural document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how reviewers assign scores during SRG review; reviewers should follow the CSR scoring procedure document for instructions on score ranges, use of criterion vs. overall scores, and any SRG-specific scoring conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Reviewers are provided to support consistent and fair evaluation of grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General reviewer responsibilities, evaluation expectations, confidentiality obligations, and best practices are outlined in the Guidelines for Reviewers document. Consult also 'Guidelines for Review of Specific Applications' for topic-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for review of specific application types
rubrics_metrics.description: There are topic- or application-type-specific guidance documents, e.g., Review of New Investigator R01s; Streamlined Review; Review of Research Involving Natural Products; Modular Grant Application and Award; Inclusion of Children as Participants; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply special instructions and considerations provided in these documents when evaluating the corresponding application types (e.g., scoring considerations for new investigators, approaches for streamlined review processes, complexity issues for natural product mixtures, modular budget formats, and inclusion of children).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of New Investigator R01s
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to the review of New Investigator R01 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains any modified expectations, comparative context, or scoring considerations for new investigators versus established investigators. Reviewers should apply these considerations when assessing investigator qualifications, significance, and approach for new investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and expectations for Streamlined Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules for when and how streamlined review occurs, including any condensed discussion or scoring procedures. Reviewers should follow the Streamlined Review document for operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Research Involving Natural Products Usually Prepared as Complex Mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for evaluating research applications involving natural products that are complex mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses evaluation challenges unique to complex mixtures (e.g., characterization, reproducibility, relevance). Reviewers should consider these factors when judging approach, feasibility, and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Grant Application and Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance related to modular budget applications and associated award processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how modular budgets are presented and any reviewer expectations for assessing budgetary information when modular formats are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children as Participants in Research Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance concerning inclusion of children as research participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when children should be included or excluded, how inclusion affects review of human-subjects protections, and relevant documentation reviewers should check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions to reviewers for evaluating research involving human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects in Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications (document dated April 5, 2002 referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers on assessment of human-subject protections, inclusion criteria, consent processes, and related ethical safeguards. Related documents include Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues, Protection of Humans, and topic-specific slides/handouts (Women, Minorities, Children).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for human and animal subjects research (applicant notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Important Notice to Applicants: Requirements for Human and Animal Subjects Research (August 29, 2002 referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets applicant-facing requirements that reviewers should be aware of when judging whether proposals meet institutional and NIH expectations for humane and ethical treatment of human and animal subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision trees to guide reviewers on human-subject protection and inclusion issues during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational flowcharts to help reviewers determine required actions, identify potential problems, or flag concerns related to human-subject protections and inclusion policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and subgroup-specific guidance (Women, Minorities, Children; Phase III trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents addressing inclusion and representation: Women in Clinical Research; Women in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials; Minorities in Clinical Research; Minorities in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials; Children in Human Subjects Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reviewer expectations for assessing whether studies adequately address inclusion of women, minorities, and children, and specify reporting or design requirements for NIH-defined Phase III trials and other clinical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on Data and Safety Monitoring Plans (DSMPs) for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess adequacy of DSMPs in proposals involving clinical trials, including monitoring procedures, stopping rules, and oversight structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest, confidentiality, and non-disclosure rules for NIH peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict Of Interest, Confidentiality And Non Disclosure Rules For NIH Peer Reviewers: Information For Reviewers Of Grant Applications And R&D Contract Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies reviewer responsibilities regarding conflicts of interest, confidentiality of application materials, non-disclosure obligations, recusal procedures, and related reporting. Linked materials include NIH Pre-Review Certification Form and NIH Post-Review Certification Form; see also the OER Conflict of Interest Page.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Pre-Review and Post-Review Certification Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Pre-Review Certification Form and NIH Post-Review Certification Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative forms reviewers must complete to certify adherence to conflict-of-interest and confidentiality rules before and after participating in peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review regulations (42 CFR Part 52h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Regulations 42 CFR Part 52h for the Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research available as Final Rules and Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/regulatory framework governing federal peer review of research grants; reviewers and administrators must comply with these regulations and the Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of initial scientific peer review (procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of Initial Scientific Peer Review (document referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and grounds for applicants to appeal initial peer review outcomes; reviewers and SROs should be familiar with appeals processes and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to investigators submitting clinical research applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance 'Advice to Investigators Submitting Clinical Research Applications' (referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendations for investigators preparing clinical research applications, including human-subjects, inclusion, and monitoring expectations that reviewers will apply during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review notes, archive, and ongoing enhancement efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH maintains Peer Review Notes, archives of Peer Review Policies & Practices documents, and has undertaken enhancement efforts (e.g., NIH 2007-2008 Peer Review Self-Study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and administrators should consult archived materials and enhancement studies to understand evolving best practices and recent changes to peer review policy.
